title: What the Public Archives Can and Cannot Tell Us About Tabernanthe iboga
content: The iboga alkaloid biosynthetic pathway was elucidated in 2026, yet the species that produces it has never been sampled genetically across its range. We inventoried every public genomic record for Tabernanthe iboga and found seven BioSamples in total: six from a single glasshouse genotype in Germany, and one 1979 herbarium specimen whose public record carries no country, locality or coordinates. Against 700 georeferenced occurrence records spanning seven Central African countries, not one sequenced or chemically characterised accession can be placed on a map. A chemotype map cannot presently be reconstructed because no published alkaloid measurement is tied to a wild collection locality. Working with what does exist, we report three results. First, we located all nine recently published pathway genes in the T. iboga v1 assembly at 97.9-100% identity and describe their genomic architecture, including three paralogues not named in the pathway literature: a coronaridine cyclase copy at 99.2% identity 16.3 kb from TiCorC1, a coronaridine 10-hydroxylase paralogue at 95.5% identity 59.9 kb from TiC10H, and a three-gene O-methyltransferase cluster on the scaffold that also carries the TiC10H pair. TiADH1 and TiADH2, which feed the voacangine and ibophyllidine branches respectively, are duplicates 92.9 kb apart on one scaffold. Second, we report a negative result: Angiosperms353 target-capture libraries cannot yield an iboga plastome. Plastid content of the one archived wild-collected library is 0.04% of reads, giving 0.4x mean depth. Third, using 174,014 callable sites across 458 single-copy nuclear loci, we provide what is to our knowledge the first quantitative estimate of genetic differentiation between two T. iboga individuals: approximately 3-4 fixed differences per kb between them, and 8-9 heterozygous sites per kb within the herbarium individual, after controlling for cytosine deamination damage.
